title: Follow-up: scanner edges — a -- after unknown or value options, and a lone dash
description: Nits 4 and 5 of the DEC-183 round-2 review of opum-ai/glyph-cli#64 (GCLI-13), recorded verbatim on GCLI-13. (4) The `--` terminator is only an operand boundary when program-level dest is operands at that point. If an unknown option or a subcommand option comes first, commander pushes `--` and the rest into unknown, and the subcommand re-parses them: its required option can consume `--` as a value and _outputHelpIfRequested finds a `--help` after it. So `glyph --json callers --bogus -- --help` and `glyph --json callers --file -- --help` print text help under --json, exit 0, where dev gave a JSON manifest. (5) A lone `-` is an operand to commander (maybeOption needs length > 1) and never a command token, so `glyph - callers --help --json` should show program help, not the callers manifest; execution paths are unaffected because commander fails on unknown command '-'.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A `--` that follows an unknown option or a subcommand option no longer turns a later `--help` into text help under --json: the output mode stays JSON on both shapes named in the review.
A lone `-` is not taken as the command token.
Existing scanner answers are unchanged and bun run check passes.
